executiveSummary: North Carolina Ports reported a cyberattack that disrupted IT systems and slowed cargo and gate operations across three facilities, triggering contingency procedures and supply-chain delays. View Article Institutional and industry reporting underscores persistent GNSS jamming/spoofing across multiple regions, with resulting erroneous positioning, near misses, and groundings; classification society guidance advises cross-checking GNSS with radar/visual fixes and maintaining alternative position-fixing. View Article Maritime Advisory Regional maritime centers recorded a surge of AIS deception incidents, degrading maritime domain awareness, sanctions/compliance screening, and navigational trust in certain waters. Supporting Report Government guidance highlights ongoing port-OT and technology supply-chain exposure (e.g., remotely maintainable cranes, logistics platforms), with recommended segmentation, MFA, monitoring, and backup validation steps for U.S. operators. Government Advisory India issued a national circular directing port facilities to integrate cyber risk management into ISPS assessments and plans, emphasizing IT/OT segregation, vendor/remote access controls, and incident reporting/exercises. Government Advisory Assessment: The collected intelligence supports an assessment that immediate operational risk is elevated for port operations in light of a recent disruptive attack, while navigation integrity risks remain persistently high in multiple regions due to GNSS interference and AIS deception. Confidence is high for the port incident and classification/government advisories, and medium for the broader regional incident tallies. Outlook: Over the next 72 hours, analysts should monitor for follow-on disruption reporting from affected U.S. ports, continuing GNSS integrity advisories, and enforcement of port cybersecurity directives. Confidence in this outlook is medium given active recovery efforts and established interference trends.

vendors: Technologies: Ship-to-shore cranes and remotely maintainable port equipment; logistics platforms (e.g., LOGINK); security screening equipment (e.g., Nuctech) - as highlighted by MARAD advisory. Government Advisory
Systems: Port IT (gates, operational support), terminal operating systems, communications networks, vendor/remote access pathways (India DGMA circular). Government Advisory

topThreats.title: North Carolina Ports cyberattack disrupts cargo and gate operations
topThreats.action: Direct operational disruption across multiple facilities with confirmed supply-chain impact Operational impact: Systems outage, delays, contingency workflows Affected: Port of Wilmington, Port of Morehead City, Charlotte Inland Port; port IT and gate systems Recommended attention: Incident-response posture, boundary monitoring during recovery, vendor/remote access review Confidence: High

topThreats.title: Persistent GNSS jamming/spoofing affecting multiple sea lanes
topThreats.action: Erroneous positioning and degraded situational awareness can lead to near misses or groundings Operational impact: Loss of GNSS integrity; need for alternate position-fixing and cross-check procedures Recommended attention: ECDIS/RADAR/visual cross-checks; integrity monitoring; crew awareness Confidence: Medium to High (industry and classification reporting)

topThreats.title: AIS deception surge degrading maritime domain awareness
topThreats.action: False identities/flags/types can mislead traffic monitoring and screening processes Operational impact: Potential confusion in congested waters; screening inaccuracies Recommended attention: Cross-verify AIS data with radar/visuals and port/VTS data; enhance anomaly alerts Confidence: Medium

topThreats.title: Port OT and technology supply-chain exposure (U.S. MARAD 2026-007)
topThreats.action: Remote maintenance and foreign-manufactured systems can expand attack surface Operational impact: Potential for operational disruption, data exposure, and compliance ramifications Recommended attention: Network segmentation, MFA, monitoring, backup validation, USCG directive compliance Confidence: High

topThreats.title: India: ISPS-aligned port cyber risk management directive
topThreats.action: Regulatory momentum requiring integrated cyber risk management at ports Operational impact: Required assessments, exercises, and vendor access governance Recommended attention: Embed cyber in PFSA/PFSP, segregate IT/OT, test recovery, formalize incident reporting Confidence: High

descriptions: AIS deception: Identity and attribute falsification to mislead observers and screening systems (behavioral observation; no specific ATT&CK ID assigned). Supporting Report
GNSS spoofing/jamming: Manipulation or denial of positioning signals causing loss of integrity (navigation safety risk; ICS ATT&CK mapping not confirmed in sources). Maritime Advisory

Port-OT exposure: External remote services and third-party access pathways to industrial assets (derived from MARAD/DGMA guidance; formal ATT&CK technique IDs not specified). Government Advisory Government Advisory

Enterprise attack surface at ports: Potential phishing, ransomware, and exploitation of remote access referenced as common vectors in port guidance (generic classes; no campaign-specific mapping). Government Advisory
